# JDK Flight Recorder (JFR) Print

JDK Flight Recorder (JFR) provide a crude way of viewing the events using the
`print` option. The `print` option, reads a JFR file and prints it content in
different formats, such as XML and JSON. It can also filter events based on a
specific type, which helps to find the needle in the haystack.

More information about the JFR `print` option is available as part of the
command’s help.

```shell
jfr --help print
```

The JFR `print` option takes the following options.

```
Print contents of a recording file

 jfr print [--xml|--json|--exact]
           [--categories <filter>]
           [--events <filter>]
           [--stack-depth <depth>]
           <file>

  --xml                   Print recording in XML format

  --json                  Print recording in JSON format

  --exact                 Pretty-print numbers and timestamps with full precision.

  --categories <filter>   Select events matching a category name.
                          The filter is a comma-separated list of names,
                          simple and/or qualified, and/or quoted glob patterns

  --events <filter>       Select events matching an event name.
                          The filter is a comma-separated list of names,
                          simple and/or qualified, and/or quoted glob patterns

  --stack-depth <depth>   Number of frames in stack traces, by default 5

  <file>                  Location of the recording file (.jfr)


Example usage:

 jfr print --events OldObjectSample recording.jfr

 jfr print --events CPULoad,GarbageCollection recording.jfr

 jfr print --categories 'GC,JVM,Java*' recording.jfr

 jfr print --exact --events 'jdk.*' --stack-depth 64 recording.jfr

 jfr print --json --events CPULoad recording.jfr
```

These options are explored in this example.

Please note that the JFR recordings files contains more information that what’s
printed. The events metadata is not shown here, as this is static information.
Please see the [JFR Metadata](../jfr-metadata/README.md) for more information
about metadata.

The JDK Mission Control provide a richer user experience as it combines the
events’ data and metadata in one view. The `jfr` command, on the other hand, is
ideal in automated systems as collection and filtering can be executed as part
of a script.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [`jq`](https://jqlang.org/)

- [`xq`](https://github.com/sibprogrammer/xq)

- [JDK Mission Control (JMC)](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/products-jmc9-downloads.html)

## JDK Mission Control (JMC)

1. Download the latest version of JMC from
   [here](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/products-jmc9-downloads.html)

2. Specify the version of Java

   When having multiple versions of Java installed, you may need to specify
   which one to be used by JMC. This can be done through the `jmc.ini` file,
   found under the `Eclipse` directory of where JMC is installed.

   Add the `-vm` option followed by the path to the `bin` directory, as shown
   next.

   ```
   ...
   -vm
   /Users/aattard/.sdkman/candidates/java/current/bin
   ...
   ```

   Please note that this file will contain other information, which is excluded
   for brevity.

## Build the application

The following examples require the application to be built.

```shell
./mvnw clean package
```

(*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created

```shell
tree --sort=name './target/libs'
```

There should be one JAR file

```
./target/libs
└── jfr-print-1.0.0.jar

1 directory, 1 file
```

Some of the following commands dump JFR files into a `jfr` directory. Make sure
that the `jfr` directory exists.

```shell
rm -rf './jfr'
mkdir -p './jfr'
```

## Use the `print` options

1. Run the application and capture the recordings

   ```shell
   java \
     -XX:StartFlightRecording=duration=30s,delay=5s,name='Print',filename='./jfr/demo.jfr' \
     -jar './target/libs/jfr-print-1.0.0.jar'
   ```

   The application will terminate automatically after 40 seconds.

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JFR file was created.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './jfr'
   ```

   The recording

   ```
   ./jfr
   └── demo.jfr

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

2. (*Optional*) Print the recording summary

   ```shell
   jfr summary './jfr/demo.jfr'
   ```

   This prints the events and their counts

   ```
    Version: 2.1
    Chunks: 1
    Start: 2077-04-27 12:34:56 (UTC)
    Duration: 30 s

    Event Type                              Count  Size (bytes)
   =============================================================
    jdk.BooleanFlag                           494         15136
    jdk.ActiveSetting                         376          9721
    jdk.SystemProcess                         277         12214
    jdk.ModuleRequire                         156          1716
   ...
   ```

3. (*Optional*) Open the flight recording file with JMC (`./jfr/demo.jfr`).

   ```shell
   jmc -open "$(pwd)/jfr/demo.jfr"
   ```

4. Print the captured events.

   ```shell
   jfr print './jfr/demo.jfr'
   ```

   This will print a lot of information.

5. Filter events by type (`--events`)

   The events can be filtered using the `--events`

   ```shell
   jfr print --events 'jdk.GCConfiguration' './jfr/demo.jfr'
   ```

   This will only print the events of type `jdk.GCConfiguration`.

   ```
   jdk.GCConfiguration {
     startTime = 12:34:56.950 (2077-04-27)
     youngCollector = "G1New"
     oldCollector = "G1Old"
     parallelGCThreads = 8
     concurrentGCThreads = 2
     usesDynamicGCThreads = true
     isExplicitGCConcurrent = false
     isExplicitGCDisabled = false
     pauseTarget = N/A
     gcTimeRatio = 12
   }

   jdk.GCConfiguration {
     startTime = 12:35:26.925 (2077-04-27)
     youngCollector = "G1New"
     oldCollector = "G1Old"
     parallelGCThreads = 8
     concurrentGCThreads = 2
     usesDynamicGCThreads = true
     isExplicitGCConcurrent = false
     isExplicitGCDisabled = false
     pauseTarget = N/A
     gcTimeRatio = 12
   }
   ```

   The previous example used the canonical event name. Alternative, just the
   name will do such as `CPUInformation` (instead of `jdk.CPUInformation`) or
   `CPUTimeStampCounter` (instead of `jdk.CPUTimeStampCounter`). Furthermore, we
   can filter on multiple events as shown below.

   ```shell
   jfr print --events 'CPUInformation,CPUTimeStampCounter' './jfr/demo.jfr'
   ```

   This will print all events of the provided types.

   ```
   jdk.CPUInformation {
     startTime = 12:34:56.949 (2077-04-27)
     cpu = "AMD Unknown x86 (HT) SSE SSE2 SSE3 SSSE3 SSE4.1 SSE4.2 SSE4A AMD64"
     description = "Brand: AMD EPYC 9J14 96-Core Processor                , Vendor: AuthenticAMD
   Family: Unknown x86 (0x19), Model: <unknown> (0x11), Stepping: 0x1
   Ext. family: 0xa, Ext. model: 0x1, Type: 0x0, Signature: 0x00a10f11
   Features: ebx: 0x05080800, ecx: 0xfffa3203, edx: 0x178bfbff
   Ext. features: eax: 0x00a10f11, ebx: 0x00000000, ecx: 0x00c003f7, edx: 0x2fd3fbff
   Supports: On-Chip FPU, Virtual Mode Extensions, Debugging Extensions, Page Size Extensions, Time Stamp Counter, Model Specific Registers, Physical Address Extension, Machine Check Exceptions, CMPXCHG8B Instruction, On-Chip APIC, Fast System Call, Memory Type Range Registers, Page Global Enable, Machine Check Architecture, Conditional Mov Instruction, Page Attribute Table, 36-bit Page Size Extension, CLFLUSH Instruction, Intel Architecture MMX Technology, Fast Float Point Save and Restore, Streaming SIMD extensions, Streaming SIMD extensions 2, Hyper Threading, Streaming SIMD Extensions 3, PCLMULQDQ, Supplemental Streaming SIMD Extensions 3, Fused Multiply-Add, CMPXCHG16B, Process-context identifiers, Streaming SIMD extensions 4.1, Streaming SIMD extensions 4.2, x2APIC, MOVBE, Popcount instruction, TSC-Deadline, AESNI, XSAVE, OSXSAVE, AVX, F16C, LAHF/SAHF instruction support, Core multi-processor legacy mode, Advanced Bit Manipulations: LZCNT, SSE4A: MOVNTSS, MOVNTSD, EXTRQ, INSERTQ, Misaligned SSE mode, SYSCALL/SYSRET, Execute Disable Bit, RDTSCP, Intel 64 Architecture"
     sockets = 1
     cores = 8
     hwThreads = 8
   }

   jdk.CPUTimeStampCounter {
     startTime = 12:34:56.949 (2077-04-27)
     fastTimeEnabled = false
     fastTimeAutoEnabled = false
     osFrequency = 1000000000 Hz
     fastTimeFrequency = 1000000000 Hz
   }
   ```

6. Filter events by category (`--categories`)

   The events can be filtered using the `--categories`

   ```shell
   jfr print --categories 'GC' './jfr/demo.jfr'
   ```

   The above will only print the events of the `GC` category.

   ```
   jdk.GCConfiguration {
     startTime = 12:34:56.950 (2077-04-27)
     youngCollector = "G1New"
     oldCollector = "G1Old"
     parallelGCThreads = 8
     concurrentGCThreads = 2
     usesDynamicGCThreads = true
     isExplicitGCConcurrent = false
     isExplicitGCDisabled = false
     pauseTarget = N/A
     gcTimeRatio = 12
   }

   jdk.GCSurvivorConfiguration {
     startTime = 12:34:56.950 (2077-04-27)
     maxTenuringThreshold = 15
     initialTenuringThreshold = 7
   }

   jdk.GCTLABConfiguration {
     startTime = 12:34:56.950 (2077-04-27)
     usesTLABs = true
     minTLABSize = 2.0 kB
     tlabRefillWasteLimit = 64 bytes
   }

   jdk.GCHeapConfiguration {
     startTime = 12:34:56.950 (2077-04-27)
     minSize = 8.0 MB
     maxSize = 7.7 GB
     initialSize = 496.0 MB
     usesCompressedOops = true
     compressedOopsMode = "Zero based"
     objectAlignment = 8 bytes
     heapAddressBits = 32
   }

   jdk.YoungGenerationConfiguration {
     startTime = 12:34:56.950 (2077-04-27)
     minSize = 1.3 MB
     maxSize = 4.6 GB
     newRatio = 2
   }

   jdk.GCConfiguration {
     startTime = 12:35:26.925 (2077-04-27)
     youngCollector = "G1New"
     oldCollector = "G1Old"
     parallelGCThreads = 8
     concurrentGCThreads = 2
     usesDynamicGCThreads = true
     isExplicitGCConcurrent = false
     isExplicitGCDisabled = false
     pauseTarget = N/A
     gcTimeRatio = 12
   }
   ```

   The events can be filtered by more than one category, comma separated.

   ```shell
   jfr print --categories 'GC,JVM' './jfr/demo.jfr'
   ```

   This will print all events that belong to either the `GC` and/or the `JVM`
   categories.

   ```
   jdk.Deoptimization {
     startTime = 12:34:56.912 (2077-04-27)
     compileId = 901
     compiler = "c2"
     method = jdk.internal.classfile.impl.SplitConstantPool.canWriteDirect(ConstantPool)
     lineNumber = 125
     bci = 15
     instruction = "if_acmpne"
     reason = "unstable_if"
     action = "reinterpret"
     eventThread = "JFR Recording Scheduler" (javaThreadId = 27)
   }
   ...
   ```

   The output is truncated for brevity.

7. Adjust the stacktrace (`--stack-depth`)

   By default, the events that also capture the stacktrace only show the first 5
   levels of the stack. The events of type `jdk.ObjectAllocationSample` comprise
   a stacktrace and can be used for this example.

   ```shell
   jfr print --events 'jdk.ObjectAllocationSample' './jfr/demo.jfr'
   ```

   At most, a stacktrace of depth 5 is shown.

   ```
   jdk.ObjectAllocationSample {
     startTime = 12:34:56.922 (2077-04-27)
     objectClass = byte[] (classLoader = bootstrap)
     weight = 3.9 MB
     eventThread = "JFR Recording Scheduler" (javaThreadId = 27)
     stackTrace = [
       java.util.Arrays.copyOf(byte[], int) line: 3537
       java.lang.AbstractStringBuilder.ensureCapacityNewCoder(byte[], byte, int, int, byte) line: 282
       java.lang.AbstractStringBuilder.append(String) line: 650
       java.lang.StringBuilder.append(String) line: 179
       jdk.jfr.internal.ClassInspector.findStaticCommitMethod() line: 98
       ...
     ]
   }

   jdk.ObjectAllocationSample {
     startTime = 12:34:56.923 (2077-04-27)
     objectClass = jdk.internal.classfile.impl.AbstractPoolEntry$MethodRefEntryImpl (classLoader = bootstrap)
     weight = 55.2 kB
     eventThread = "JFR Recording Scheduler" (javaThreadId = 27)
     stackTrace = [
       jdk.internal.classfile.impl.SplitConstantPool.methodRefEntry(ClassEntry, NameAndTypeEntry) line: 572
       java.lang.classfile.constantpool.ConstantPoolBuilder.methodRefEntry(ClassDesc, String, MethodTypeDesc) line: 329
       java.lang.classfile.CodeBuilder.invoke(Opcode, ClassDesc, String, MethodTypeDesc, boolean) line: 560
       java.lang.classfile.CodeBuilder.invokestatic(ClassDesc, String, MethodTypeDesc) line: 2628
       jdk.jfr.internal.util.Bytecode.invokestatic(CodeBuilder, ClassDesc, Bytecode$MethodDesc) line: 125
       ...
     ]
   }

   jdk.ObjectAllocationSample {
     startTime = 12:34:56.939 (2077-04-27)
     objectClass = int[] (classLoader = bootstrap)
     weight = 970.3 kB
     eventThread = "JFR Recording Scheduler" (javaThreadId = 27)
     stackTrace = [
       jdk.internal.classfile.impl.EntryMap.<init>(int, float) line: 77
       jdk.internal.classfile.impl.SplitConstantPool.map() line: 182
       jdk.internal.classfile.impl.SplitConstantPool.tryFindClassOrInterface(int, ClassDesc) line: 403
       jdk.internal.classfile.impl.SplitConstantPool.classEntryForClassOrInterface(ClassDesc) line: 438
       jdk.internal.classfile.impl.SplitConstantPool.classEntry(ClassDesc) line: 514
       ...

   ```

   This can be adjusted using the `--stack-depth` option.

   ```shell
   jfr print --stack-depth 1 --events 'jdk.ObjectAllocationSample' './jfr/demo.jfr'
   ```

   This will only print a stacktrace of 1 entry.

   ```
   jdk.ObjectAllocationSample {
     startTime = 12:34:56.922 (2077-04-27)
     objectClass = byte[] (classLoader = bootstrap)
     weight = 3.9 MB
     eventThread = "JFR Recording Scheduler" (javaThreadId = 27)
     stackTrace = [
       java.util.Arrays.copyOf(byte[], int) line: 3537
       ...
     ]
   }

   jdk.ObjectAllocationSample {
     startTime = 12:34:56.923 (2077-04-27)
     objectClass = jdk.internal.classfile.impl.AbstractPoolEntry$MethodRefEntryImpl (classLoader = bootstrap)
     weight = 55.2 kB
     eventThread = "JFR Recording Scheduler" (javaThreadId = 27)
     stackTrace = [
       jdk.internal.classfile.impl.SplitConstantPool.methodRefEntry(ClassEntry, NameAndTypeEntry) line: 572
       ...

   }

   jdk.ObjectAllocationSample {
     startTime = 12:34:56.939 (2077-04-27)
     objectClass = int[] (classLoader = bootstrap)
     weight = 970.3 kB
     eventThread = "JFR Recording Scheduler" (javaThreadId = 27)
     stackTrace = [
       jdk.internal.classfile.impl.EntryMap.<init>(int, float) line: 77
       ...
     ]
   }
   ```

   The stacktrace depth can be adjusted accordingly.

8. Print the captured events as JSON (`--json`).

   The output can be JSON formatted by using the `--json`

   ```shell
   jfr print \
     --json \
     --events 'CPUInformation,CPUTimeStampCounter' \
     './jfr/demo.jfr' \
     | jq
   ```

   The above will only print the events of type `jdk.CPUInformation` and
   `CPUTimeStampCounter` (because of the `--events` option) in JSON format
   (because of the `--json` option).

   ```json
   {
     "recording": {
       "events": [

           "values": {
             "startTime": "2077-04-27T12:34:56.949749611Z",
             "cpu": "AMD Unknown x86 (HT) SSE SSE2 SSE3 SSSE3 SSE4.1 SSE4.2 SSE4A AMD64",
             "description": "Brand: AMD EPYC 9J14 96-Core Processor                , Vendor: AuthenticAMD\nFamily: Unknown x86 (0x19), Model: <unknown> (0x11), Stepping: 0x1\nExt. family: 0xa, Ext. model: 0x1, Type: 0x0, Signature: 0x00a10f11\nFeatures: ebx: 0x05080800, ecx: 0xfffa3203, edx: 0x178bfbff\nExt. features: eax: 0x00a10f11, ebx: 0x00000000, ecx: 0x00c003f7, edx: 0x2fd3fbff\nSupports: On-Chip FPU, Virtual Mode Extensions, Debugging Extensions, Page Size Extensions, Time Stamp Counter, Model Specific Registers, Physical Address Extension, Machine Check Exceptions, CMPXCHG8B Instruction, On-Chip APIC, Fast System Call, Memory Type Range Registers, Page Global Enable, Machine Check Architecture, Conditional Mov Instruction, Page Attribute Table, 36-bit Page Size Extension, CLFLUSH Instruction, Intel Architecture MMX Technology, Fast Float Point Save and Restore, Streaming SIMD extensions, Streaming SIMD extensions 2, Hyper Threading, Streaming SIMD Extensions 3, PCLMULQDQ, Supplemental Streaming SIMD Extensions 3, Fused Multiply-Add, CMPXCHG16B, Process-context identifiers, Streaming SIMD extensions 4.1, Streaming SIMD extensions 4.2, x2APIC, MOVBE, Popcount instruction, TSC-Deadline, AESNI, XSAVE, OSXSAVE, AVX, F16C, LAHF/SAHF instruction support, Core multi-processor legacy mode, Advanced Bit Manipulations: LZCNT, SSE4A: MOVNTSS, MOVNTSD, EXTRQ, INSERTQ, Misaligned SSE mode, SYSCALL/SYSRET, Execute Disable Bit, RDTSCP, Intel 64 Architecture",
   ```

9.  Print the captured events as XML (`--xml`).

   The output can be XML formatted by using the `--xml`

   ```shell
   jfr print \
     --xml \
     --events 'CPUInformation,CPUTimeStampCounter' \
     './jfr/demo.jfr' \
     | xq
   ```

   The above will only print the events of type `jdk.CPUInformation` and
   `CPUTimeStampCounter` (because of the `--events` option) in XML format
   (because of the `--xml` option).

   ```xml
   <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
   <recording xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
     <events>
       <event type="jdk.CPUInformation">
         <value name="startTime">2077-04-27T12:34:56.949749611Z</value>
         <value name="cpu">AMD Unknown x86 (HT) SSE SSE2 SSE3 SSSE3 SSE4.1 SSE4.2 SSE4A AMD64</value>
         <value name="description"><![CDATA[Brand: AMD EPYC 9J14 96-Core Processor                , Vendor: AuthenticAMD
   Family: Unknown x86 (0x19), Model: <unknown> (0x11), Stepping: 0x1
   ```
